name: [TrueInterview Case 1] overlapping phrases form one highlighted block
input: document = 'Read red green blue today.'; sources = ['red green', 'green blue']
test:
tagged_document, counts, citations = highlight_with_citations('Read red green blue today.', ['red green', 'green blue'])
assert tagged_document == 'Read <yellow>red green blue</yellow>[0][1] today.'
assert counts == {0: 1, 1: 1}
assert citations == [[0, 1]]

name: [TrueInterview Case 2] citation order uses global frequency then source index
input: document = 'Alpha beta gamma; beta gamma delta.'; sources = ['beta gamma', 'gamma', 'delta', 'beta']
test:
tagged_document, counts, citations = highlight_with_citations('Alpha beta gamma; beta gamma delta.', ['beta gamma', 'gamma', 'delta', 'beta'])
assert tagged_document == 'Alpha <yellow>beta gamma</yellow>[0][1][3]; <yellow>beta gamma delta</yellow>[0][1][3][2].'
assert counts == {0: 2, 1: 2, 2: 1, 3: 2}
assert citations == [[0, 1, 3], [0, 1, 3, 2]]

name: [TrueInterview Case 3] matching is case-sensitive and duplicate sources stay distinct
test:
tagged_document, counts, citations = highlight_with_citations('blueprint BLUE blue', ['blue', 'blue', 'BLUE'])
assert tagged_document == 'blueprint <yellow>BLUE blue</yellow>[0][1][2]'
assert counts == {0: 1, 1: 1, 2: 1}
assert citations == [[0, 1, 2]]

name: [Prompt example] global frequency orders citations across blocks
input: document = 'A red bird sings while a red fish swims.'; sources = ['red bird', 'bird sings', 'red', 'fish']
test:
tagged_document, counts, citations = highlight_with_citations('A red bird sings while a red fish swims.', ['red bird', 'bird sings', 'red', 'fish'])
assert tagged_document == 'A <yellow>red bird sings</yellow>[2][0][1] while a <yellow>red fish</yellow>[2][3] swims.'
assert counts == {0: 1, 1: 1, 2: 2, 3: 1}
assert citations == [[2, 0, 1], [2, 3]]

name: [Prompt rule] whitespace-adjacent matches merge and no matches preserve the document
input: whitespace adjacency and a document with no valid occurrence
test:
tagged_document, counts, citations = highlight_with_citations('alpha  beta, gamma', ['alpha', 'beta', 'gamma'])
assert tagged_document == '<yellow>alpha  beta</yellow>[0][1], <yellow>gamma</yellow>[2]'
assert counts == {0: 1, 1: 1, 2: 1}
assert citations == [[0, 1], [2]]

tagged_document, counts, citations = highlight_with_citations('unrelated_text', ['related', 'text'])
assert tagged_document == 'unrelated_text'
assert counts == {0: 0, 1: 0}
assert citations == []
